paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this one, friend. God doesn't just tell Aaron and his sons to go serve Him. He walks Moses through every step of making them ready: water, garments, oil, blood and a whole lot of offerings. The priests don't make themselves ready. God does it, and He says so Himself: "I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve Me as priests." (Exodus 29:44)

Now look at what the blood and the sin offering are doing here. Even the priests need atonement before they can stand near a holy God, and the text says the bull is "a sin offering" (Exodus 29:14). Nobody earns their way in. I get a little choked up about that, because I know what it is to be picked up when I had nothing to bring. The same God who reached into my junk drawer is the One who makes His people ready.

And here's WHY He does it all. He says He brought Israel out of Egypt "so that I might dwell among them." (Exodus 29:46) The whole point was never the lambs, the garments or the oil. The point was God with His people, meeting them and speaking to them (Exodus 29:42-43). So when you open the Word, baker, you're not walking into a room where you have to get everything perfect. You're walking toward a God who wants to be near you.
